<h1 id="Hamon-(1961)-Temperature-Based-PET">Hamon (1961) Temperature-Based PET<a class="anchor-link" href="#Hamon-(1961)-Temperature-Based-PET">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Experiment 035</strong> — Python control baseline aligned with primal <code>science.et0_hamon</code> and Rust <code>validate_hamon</code>.</p>
</div>

<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Theory">Theory<a class="anchor-link" href="#Theory">¶</a></h2><p>Hamon PET uses mean temperature and day length (possible sunshine hours). This notebook follows the <strong>Lu et al. (2005)</strong> formulation used in <code>hamon_pet.py</code>.</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{PET} = 0.1651 \, N \, \rho_{\mathrm{sat}} \, K_{\mathrm{PEC}}$$</p>
<p>with saturated vapour pressure $e_s$ (kPa), $\rho_{\mathrm{sat}} = 216.7\, e_s/(T+273.3)$ g m⁻³, $N$ daylight hours, and $K_{\mathrm{PEC}}=1$.</p>
<p>An equivalent textbook form is PET = 0.55 × (N/12)² × e_s(T)/100 × 25.4 under algebraic rearrangement of constants (see Lu et al. 2005; Hamon 1961).</p>
<p><strong>Citation:</strong> Hamon WR (1961) <em>J Hydraulics Div ASCE</em> 87(HY3):107–120; Lu J et al. (2005) <em>J Am Water Resour Assoc</em> 41(3):621–633.</p>
</div>
</div>
